Plotters: what is covered and how to add more

Source: vignettes/adding-plotters.Rmd
adding-plotters.Rmd

rvis gives many htmlwidgets plotting packages one calling convention: rvisPlot(type, plotter, ...) calls the wrapper function named <plotter>.<type>(). This page lists the plotters rvis covers today, the packages planned next (mainly from the htmlwidgets gallery), and how to add a plotter.

Plotters planned

These htmlwidgets packages are not wrapped yet. The table gives the chart types each would add and the guide its examples would go to. Packages marked dashboard only already have dashboard output types, but have no rvisPlot() wrapper yet. (Any htmlwidget can be a dashboard output with a package::fooOutput item type, see step 4 below.) Packages marked not on CRAN were archived on CRAN, so a CRAN version of rvis cannot depend on them.

How to add a plotter

A plotter is a set of wrapper functions <plotter>.<type>() in one file R/<plotter>.R. The steps below show a simplified version of the apexcharter bar chart (the full wrappers are in R/apexcharter.R).

1. Default settings

Each wrapper has a list of default settings, built on the package-wide defset with %<==>% (which merges two lists, the right one winning). dimclass gives the valid classes of each dimension, multiples the dimensions that accept several columns (series) and essentials the dimensions that must be given.

apexcharter.bar.defset = defset %<==>% list(
  dimclass   = list(x = valid.nominal.classes, y = valid.numeric.classes, color = valid.classes),
  multiples  = c('y', 'color'),
  essentials = c('x', 'y')
)

2. The wrapper

A wrapper takes the data, the dimensions (column names or lists of them) and config, and returns the htmlwidget. The common steps are:

  • return NULL for empty data, and stop with a clear message if the plotting package is not installed;
  • merge config over the defaults and check it with verifyConfig() (which reads the valid settings of the plotter from the properties table, see step 3);
  • prepareAesthetics() turns the dimensions into column labels (L) and aesthetics;
  • prepare4Plot() builds the table to plot: it selects and renames columns, checks their classes and adds colours;
  • the plotting package is called with the prepared table and the settings.
apexcharter.bar = function(obj, x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL, config = NULL, ...){
  # Verifications:
  if (is.empty(obj)){return(NULL)}
  assert(requireNamespace('apexcharter', quietly = TRUE), "Package apexcharter is not installed!", err_src = match.call()[[1]])
  config = apexcharter.bar.defset %<==>% (config %>% verify('list', default = list(), varname = 'config')) %>%
    verifyConfig(plotter = 'apexcharter')

  # Preparing Aesthetics:
  a = prepareAesthetics(x = x, y = y, color = color)
  L = a$labels

  # Preparing Table:
  obj %<>% prepare4Plot(a$aesthetics, config = config)

  # One row per category and series:
  long = data.frame(category = rep(obj[, L$x], length(L$y)),
                    value    = unlist(obj[, unlist(L$y)], use.names = FALSE),
                    series   = rep(unlist(L$y), each = nrow(obj)))

  apexcharter::apex(long, apexcharter::aes(x = category, y = value, fill = series), type = 'column', ...) %>%
    apexcharter::ax_title(text = config$title)
}

rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "apexcharter", obj = deaths, x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male")) then calls it. A helper function of the file must not be named <plotter>.<something>, or it would be callable as a chart type: name it <plotter>Something instead.

3. Settings in the properties table

The settings a plotter accepts, with their class, default and valid values, are rows of data/properties.csv (columns plotters, Property, Class, Default, Domain), which is also saved as data/properties.RData and documented in the configuration reference:

plotters,Property,Class,Default,Domain
apexcharter,title,character,,
apexcharter,legend.position,character,bottom,top right bottom left

4. Dashboard output

Nothing needs to be added for dashboards: the output function of the package is used directly as a package::function item type, and its render function is found by name (apexchartOutput is rendered by renderApexchart):

chart:
  type: apexcharter::apexchartOutput
  height: 300px
  service: rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "apexcharter", obj = deaths, x = "age", y = "rural_male")

If the render function does not follow the fooOutput / renderFoo naming, give it in field render.

5. Documentation

  • a version history line in the header of R/<plotter>.R and in R/rvis.R;
  • the wrapper in the chart-type tables of the reference;
  • examples in the topic guide of each chart type, evaluated only if the package is installed: ```{r, eval=has_plotter("apexcharter")};
  • the package under Suggests in DESCRIPTION.
